note: The Cottonwood population passes the lower Fraser very early, April-May (Candy et al. 2002, p. 22). The window ends the day before NuSEDS's median start of spawning (08-10), as BULK's migration ends where its spawning starts; NuSEDS's median stream arrival is 08-01 (23 population-years). NuSEDS's start of spawning is an estimate, not the first spawner seen: read as the bulk of spawning it is the same day, 08-10, and no record has the survey to stand for an edge (research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).

NuSEDS release 20260601: median START_SPAWN_DT_FROM to median END_SPAWN_DT_TO (else END_SPAWN_DT_FROM) over 35 and 36 population-years, 1953-2009, of three populations on streams wholly in COTR by FWA watershed code (data-raw/timing_nuseds.R, scripts/logs/timing/20261118_timing_nuseds.txt): the Swift River (a Cottonwood tributary) 08-05 to 09-01 (21 years, 1953-1974), Naver Creek 08-13 to 09-10 (10 years) and a second Swift River population 07-28 to 09-20 (4 years). The Cottonwood River's own records carry no spawn dates, and most dated years are before 1975. Candy et al. 2002 (Appendix 1) give 2001 peak spawning weeks of 8/21-8/28 for the Cottonwood and 8/19-8/26 for Naver Creek. NuSEDS's start and end dates are estimates, not the first and last spawners seen (19 of these 35 starts fall on DFO's five-day grid, and 12 of the 32 with a survey's first day precede it), so they support the middle of this window and cannot test its edges. Read as the bulk of spawning (bins as midpoints, records whose adults were present) it runs 08-10 to 09-05 over 35 and 36 population-years (1953-2009), peaking about 08-24 (40 peaks, 1953-2008); no record has the survey to stand for an edge (scripts/logs/timing/20261124_timing_nuseds.txt, research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).
